races.title: State Assembly, District 63
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Natasha Johnson
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 63 since September 2025, after winning a special election. Lake Elsinore city councilmember 2012–2025, serving three one-year terms as mayor. Worked in personal finance and banking, and most recently in marketing for Navy Federal Credit Union.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California endorsed her in the 2026 race (Ballotpedia list of endorsements and voter guide recommendations).
Reform California endorsed her in the 2026 race (Ballotpedia list).
Her predecessor, Bill Essayli, endorsed her for the 2025 special election the day after he resigned.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Natasha Johnson was born or raised, or when she came to California. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2025 or 2026, and the pages we read include no campaign-site statements or interviews on her policy positions. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, and no documented controversies. Her record on property taxes, gun policy, abortion, school choice, police funding and land ownership is not covered in the sources we could read. Her only documented action on these topics is the 2018 council vote on SB 54.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lake Elsinore city councilmember from 2012 to 2025, including three terms as mayor and three as mayor pro tem; Assembly member since September 2025; earlier work in personal finance and banking, and in marketing at Navy Federal Credit Union.
qual.why: She has 13 years of local elected office and about a year in the Assembly, plus a finance career. That supports a score above the middle band, but short of the top because her state legislative service is brief and no law or budget-policy career is documented.

workers-first.evidence: In 2018, as a Lake Elsinore city councilmember, she voted with the unanimous council to express the city's opposition to SB 54, the state law that limits state and local police cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Kevin Akin
cands.bio: Retired steam engineer from Riverside who has also worked as a carpenter and a steelworker. He is listed as chair of the Peace and Freedom Party of California. He has held no elected office. He ran for state Treasurer in 2018 and ran for Assembly District 63 as a write-in in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed on two Sway voter-guide recommendations: CrowdSourceCarrie Voting Guide, and "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace).
His campaign site says Fauzia Rizvi, the Democrat who ran for Assembly District 63 in 2022, cast her ballot for him. This is a vote, not a formal endorsement.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Akin holding any elected or appointed office, so there are no bills or official actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, homestead property-tax relief specifically, abortion, guns, police pay or school choice. He wants taxes shifted from working people and the poor to the very wealthy, including property taxes, but he does not say he would cut or end homestead taxes. He also supports free public education from preschool through university, which is not the same as school choice. His claim to chair the Peace and Freedom Party comes from Ballotpedia, and we found no party page confirming it. The Q&A he gave to Southern California News Group was linked from his campaign site, but we could not read it. His work history and local ties are self-reported, with no independent reporting found.

local.label: Roots 100: Akin says he was born in Riverside and raised in the area, and has lived in his current house in the 63rd District for 52 years. His campaign statement says he was born and raised in Western Riverside County.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He worked as a carpenter (about five years), a steelworker (about ten years) and a hospital boiler-room steam engineer (over 20 years, to 2005), and is now retired. He describes unpaid party and community volunteer work and was a candidate for state Treasurer in 2018. He has held no elected or paid public office.
qual.why: His work record is real but in trades unrelated to writing law or budgets, and he has no legislative, local elected or policy-career experience. Party and volunteer roles are not scored.

clean-money.evidence: Akin says he refuses contributions from corporations and corporate PACs and wants sharply limited corporate-PAC and independent-committee money in politics.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Akin says the 63rd District needs greenspace and decent jobs, not warehouses and environmental destruction.

workers-first.evidence: Akin calls the Trump administration's actions against immigrants a complete reversal of American tradition, which goes against the plank's call for strong immigration enforcement.
